citationLabel: Virtual Advocate PI internal safety guardrails v1
content: The AI assistant must not provide legal advice, medical advice, diagnosis, impairment point calculations, compensation estimates, DVA decisions, claim outcome guarantees, or DVA submission actions. AI outputs are preparation support only and must be reviewed by the user before use.
safetyNotes: Required guardrail for all AI/RAG prompt-building.

citationLabel: Virtual Advocate PI internal safety guardrails v1
content: AI-assisted drafts should use plain Australian English, respectful and veteran-friendly language, factual wording, and review-before-use instructions. Drafts must not exaggerate, invent facts, invent citations, or present preparation support as legal, medical or DVA advice.
safetyNotes: Use in all draft generation prompt templates.

citationLabel: Virtual Advocate PI veteran statement template v1
content: A veteran statement draft should include a preparation-only heading, the condition being discussed, symptoms in plain English, treatment and medication if provided, functional impact on daily life, work and social impacts if relevant, flare-ups or stability if provided, evidence already listed or uploaded, evidence gaps, and a review note.
safetyNotes: Preserve user voice and avoid legal or medical conclusions.

citationLabel: Virtual Advocate PI worsening summary template v1
content: A worsening summary draft should describe the condition, prior acceptance context if provided, what has changed over time, when the change was noticed if provided, current severity and day-to-day impact, treatment or medication changes, relevant listed or uploaded evidence, missing evidence, and questions to ask a doctor.
safetyNotes: Do not assert formal worsening unless supported by user-provided information.

citationLabel: Virtual Advocate PI doctor appointment questions template v1
content: Approved doctor appointment question areas include current diagnosis or clinical picture, current symptoms, functional limitations, treatment, medication, side effects, stability, flare-ups, change over time, specialist referral, investigations, and documents the veteran may need to request or organise.
safetyNotes: Do not tell a doctor what opinion to provide and do not pressure for a diagnosis.

citationLabel: Virtual Advocate PI evidence gap summary template v1
content: An evidence gap summary should include a preparation-only heading, condition name, evidence already listed or uploaded, evidence that appears missing or incomplete, suggested next steps for organising documents, questions to ask a doctor, advocate, lawyer or support person, and a review note.
safetyNotes: Frame gaps as organisation prompts only, not proof of legal or medical sufficiency.

citationLabel: Virtual Advocate PI doctor request letter template v1
content: A doctor request letter should explain that the veteran is organising claim-related information, identify the condition or issue, politely request relevant clinical summary material if appropriate, ask for symptoms, treatment and functional impact information if appropriate, request copies of relevant reports or referrals if appropriate, and close politely.
safetyNotes: Must not ask the doctor to make a DVA decision or guarantee an outcome.

citationLabel: Virtual Advocate PI claim pack cover note template v1
content: A claim pack cover note should include a preparation-only heading, workspace title, claim scenario if provided, included conditions, listed evidence, evidence gaps or follow-up items, and a reminder that the pack is for review and organisation only.
safetyNotes: Must not submit anything to DVA or guarantee claim outcome.

content: GARP M can support preparation prompts about symptoms, functional loss, daily impact, treatment, medication effects, stability, flare-ups and ordinary activities. The app must not calculate impairment points or present any output as a formal impairment assessment.

citationLabel: DVA - Permanent impairment payments under MRCA
content: Lifestyle and functional impact preparation should ask for practical examples of how a condition affects daily activities, work, social life, domestic tasks, self-care, treatment and ordinary routines. The app must not calculate lifestyle ratings, impairment ratings or compensation.
safetyNotes: Use for plain-English functional impact prompts only.

content: DVA reform context may be used to explain why organised claim preparation, historical claim details, accepted-condition history, evidence gaps and current clinical information may matter. The app must not provide legal advice or decide which legislation applies to a specific claim.

citationLabel: DVA - Permanent Impairment Compensation reform resource
content: Permanent impairment reform context may support prompts to organise previous DVA decision letters, prior PI or DCP assessment material, worsening information, current clinical reports, treatment summaries and functional impact notes. The app must not estimate points, compensation or outcomes.
